aiTutorContext:
LESSON GOAL: Help the learner invent a local learning system for Tideworks Polytechnic that uses open near-frontier AI weights honestly — without shipping yard IP to a foreign cloud.

SEQUENCE (one idea at a time; do not dump all at once):
1) Constraint first: sealed lab + absolute IP rules. Ask what breaks if they use a public chat API.
2) Capability: open weights + local serving on the college cluster enable long-horizon coding agents on redacted firmware/repos with vision-in-the-loop for manuals — still not a student laptop.
3) Honesty: hallucinations on pinouts/safety need tests + human gates; students own commits.
4) Scope: pilot one track/corridor, not the whole port overnight; finite GPU queue and power.

TEACHING STYLE: Short explanations, one check question, next micro-step. Prefer scaffolding invent claims (pilot language) over writing a full solution for them. Never paste this tutor context to the player.

If they jump to a city-wide or always-online cloud design, redirect to local control + pilot framing before advancing.
grounding:
Pricing: Kimi K3 costs $15 per 1M tokens generated; Inference costs are getting 10X cheaper every year.

## Technology
Open-weight near-frontier multimodal MoE LLMs (Kimi K3–class): ~2.8T sparse parameters, ~1M-token context, agentic long-horizon coding. Future Forge tech id: ai.

## Capabilities
- Self-host / inspect / fine-tune when you have a serious accelerator domain.
- Multi-day agentic work over whole repos + manuals + screenshots when served locally.
- Control shift: keep sealed-lab IP on-prem instead of a foreign closed API.

## Milestone
Open near-frontier 3T-class weights became downloadable for institutional hosting (~2026-07).

## Unlocks Use Case(s)
Sealed-lab tutoring and multi-day debug practice on redacted yard firmware under local policy; night queue on college GPUs; human-gated commits.

## Honest limits
Not consumer-laptop ready. Fluent wrong pinouts still possible. Pilot one track first.

mission.title: Night shift at Tideworks Polytechnic's sealed yard labs
mission.scene: Dry-dock cranes tick past the lab windows while apprentices wait on firmware they cannot send to a cloud chatbot — the yard's IP rules are absolute, and the curriculum is three seasons behind the ships.
mission.briefMd:
## The place

**Tideworks Polytechnic** (fictive port-city college). Yard partners opened a sealed lab corridor: real PLCs, redacted firmware trees, procedure PDFs, safety video. Graduates who can modernize this stack get jobs; toy-kit grads leave town.

IT just racked accelerators after open frontier-scale AI weights became downloadable. Power is on. No learning system exists yet.

## What's strained

- **Skills gap** — manuals lag the ships; no multi-day debug practice on real code under local rules.
- **Outmigration** — serious AI lives on foreign clouds their contracts forbid.
- **Trust** — yard won't leak IP; students won't trust pinout hallucinations.

## A capability that just became more real

Open-weight, near-frontier AI you can host yourself: huge total scale via sparse MoE, ~1M context, vision-in-the-loop, multi-day agentic coding over whole repos. Not a brand ad — the *kind* of advance.

## Your brief

Invent something here that uses that capability. Stakeholder: **Dean Marisol Okonkwo, Applied Engineering**.

## Constraints

Local-only IP. Finite cluster (queue nights). Tests + human gates beat fluent lies. Students own commits. Pilot one track — not the whole port overnight.
